check_text:
protocol.py: 1 biology problem (1 note).

1. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 7 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and
3 more went in (20% of the well)
   line 53:  p20.dispense(5, plate[dst])
   At line 53 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 3 more to wells A1,
   B1, C1, D1, E1, F1 and G1 in slot 3, which already held master mix (this line did it 7
   times). The addition was 20% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run
   ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so
   what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually
   vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1 and G1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1 and G1 in slot 3 after line 53: `mix_after=(5, 20)`
   on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the
   well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [9a4a1ff5745c]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
